summary: Trace-dependent applications of the Part I q-Hodge formalism: descend chosen trace pairs, prove the perfected spherical-lift criterion for the existing naive filtration, compare the framed trace filtration with the canonical algebraic one, and transport number-field Habiro specializations across the genuine-fixed-point comparison. Trace, prismatic and coefficient constructions remain with their existing owners.

nodes.title: Habiro descent of a chosen trace q-Hodge pair
nodes.statement: On the compatible structured-lift inputs of RT.4:q-Hodge satisfying the global conditions below, define traceHabiro(R,L) = H(R,F_tr(L)) by applying the Part I Habiro descent functor to the imported trace pair. Its h-completion is qHdg(R,F_tr), and its q^m−1 reduction has the exhaustive ascending q-Witt filtration with gr_i ≃ Σ^(−i) qW_m dR^i_{R/A}. On morphisms of the chosen lifted diagrams it is the composite functor; a bare map of underlying rings does not specify such a morphism. If the supplied local structures satisfy KU Remark 4.28 for n≥2, the output inherits E_(n−1); the comparison of the completed filtration with trace graded pieces has that same specified level.
hypotheses: A is a perfectly covered Λ-ring. Each Â_p has the p-complete connective E∞ spherical lift of KU 3.1(tC_p), including the π₀ Frobenius identification and the S¹-equivariant E∞ Tate-valued Frobenius, not merely a map of underlying spectra.

R is quasi-lci over A and has bounded p^∞-torsion for every p. At each p choose either the connective spherical E₂ lift of KU 3.2(E₂), or its E₁ resolution: p-torsion-free R̂_p, p-quasisyntomic semiperfect-mod-p cover, and the full augmented cosimplicial connective E₁ lift of the p-completed Čech nerve. Choices may differ at different primes.
Retain KU 4.18a(R2): R̂₂ has the E₁ resolution data, automatic when 2 is a unit. Compatible gluing and the lifted morphisms are imported from RT, with no assertion of a canonical lift of arbitrary R.

The imported F_tr is the entire q-Hodge pair with (a),(b),(c),(c_p) and their coherences. The trace formula identifies its filtration completion, not the uncompleted pair. In Rees notation h=q−1=βt, with β in filtration degree +1 and t in degree −1.
proofSteps: Use RT spherical-lift, compatible-spherical-lifts and q-hodge-global to obtain the pair with every coherence. The completed comparison is Σ^(−2i) gr^i_(even,hS¹) TC⁻(ku_R/ku_A).

Apply the already constructed Part I habiro-descent to that pair. Its factorial-indexed partial descents and h-completion are supplied by the-habiro-hodge-complex and the-q-hodge-complex; do not reconstruct TC⁻ or the Habiro completion.

Apply the imported q-Witt filtration theorem to each derived q^m−1 reduction. This gives the graded theorem and the m=1 conjugate filtration, without replacing the reduction by an unfiltered q-Witt complex.
Compose the supplied maps of pairs and the descent functor, obtaining identity and composition laws. Use q-hodge-multiplicativity and multiplicative-upgrades only with the stated E_n data.

The E₁-resolution construction also works at p=2 with its actual Čech and torsion hypotheses. No universal replacement of a spherical lift by a ku-lift is made.

api.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.traceHabiro

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.traceHabiro_etale

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.traceHabiro_unitFiltration

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.traceHabiro_polynomial

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.traceHabiro_mOne
tests.statement: At m=1 the ascending reduction filtration is conjugate with gr_i=Σ^(−i)dR^i. It is not the descending Hodge filtration F_tr/β, even though both reduce along h at the underlying coefficient level.

nodes.title: Spherical lift after perfection and the naive filtration
nodes.statement: Let p be any prime, A a p-complete p-completely perfectly covered δ-ring and R a p-complete p-torsion-free p-quasi-lci A-algebra with R/p relatively semiperfect over A. Put R_∞=(R⊗_A A_∞)^∧_p for the perfected base. If R_∞ has a connective p-complete spherical E₁ lift, the ordinary-preimage naive filtration of Part I satisfies F_naive/β ≃ fil_Hdg dR_{R/A}. Together with its already constructed zeroth, rational and p-rational data this is the local q-Hodge pair used in the canonical quasi-regular section. The filtration itself is defined without choosing a spherical lift.
hypotheses: The spherical lift is of R_∞, not necessarily of R; it is used to prove the existing filtration is a deformation.
The derived (p,h)-completed flat base change is used; an uncompleted ordinary tensor product is not a replacement.
The mod-β quotient is the filtered quotient. The assertion holds also at p=2 using the identity-cover E₁ theorem, with no blanket 2-invertibility assumption.
proofSteps: The Part I injectivity theorem supplies F_naive/β ↪ fil_Hdg dR, so only surjectivity remains.

By Part I flat-base-change, pull back along the p-completely faithfully flat A→A_∞. This reduces to a perfect δ-base. Its vanishing relative cotangent complex identifies the relevant q-de Rham and de Rham objects with those over ℤ_p, as in the proof of QH 4.22.

Apply RT quasi-regular-quotients (KU 4.17) to the identity cover of R_∞ over ℤ_p. Its E₁ spherical lift and semiperfect reduction supply the local comparison at every p, with KU 4.14 covering p=2. The resulting trace filtration is exactly the ordinary naive preimage.
Descend surjectivity by the same completed faithfully flat base change. Keep the Part I comparison maps; no arbitrary filtered equivalence or global uniqueness of chosen filtrations is used.

sources.locator: Construction 4.21 and Theorem 4.22(b), p.62; Lemmas 4.26–4.27 and proof of Theorem 4.22, pp.64–66
sources.match: The proof reduces by completed flat perfection to the identity-cover trace theorem; the hypothesis concerns the perfected base change.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.14 and Remark 4.15, p.43, proof pp.43–45; Theorem 4.17, pp.45–46
sources.match: The E₁ identity-cover filtration is the lift-independent static preimage and is a deformation, including at 2.
Higher powers give sufficient spherical lifts only in the stated prime ranges, while a toric exponent-one example also has a lift.

acceptance: The perfected free-δ exponent-one quotient has no conclusion from this theorem merely because an E₁ ku-lift exists: its naive deformation already fails.

A higher-power perfect-regular presentation with exponents ≥2 supplies the cited spherical E₁ lift for odd p; at p=2 this route requires even exponents ≥4. The independent Part I algebraic higher-power theorem still covers all exponents ≥2 at 2.

For A=ℤ_p[x]^∧_p with δ(x)=0 and R=A/(x−1), the spherical polynomial evaluation at x=1 gives the required lift after perfection. The elements ∏_{0≤i<n}(x−q^i)/[n]_q! reduce to (x−1)^n/n!, exhibiting the Hodge lifts.
The local statement feeds Part I’s arithmetic pullback criterion prime by prime. Its rational combined-filtration corner must still be retained.

nodes.title: Canonical and framed trace filtrations agree
nodes.statement: Let A be a perfectly covered Λ-ring with a chosen spherical cyclotomic base as in KU 3.1 and 4.18, and let □:A[x₁,…,x_d]→S be an étale framing as in KU 6.7. Assume every prime ≤d is a unit in S, so the Part I canonical smooth pair is defined on this framing. Use its canonical étale spherical lift S_{S,□} and the KU 6.10 framed trace comparison, with that theorem’s chosen coherent resolutions. Then the completed trace filtration identifies with the completed canonical filtration through the coordinate complex: in cohomological degree j its i-th step is h^max(i−j,0)Ω^j_{S/A}[[h]]. Pulling back the specified coordinate equivalence along qdR→qΩ identifies the two chosen pairs, including all comparison data, and hence their Habiro descents. This is a comparison on the full common domain, with no extra universal inversion of 2.
hypotheses: The entire spherical base structure of KU is required. Merely being perfectly covered is insufficient to assert existence of a spherical base.

The RT input requested here is KU 6.10 for all framed smooth A-algebras, not only the already planned ℤ[x] example. Its proof must retain the coherent prime-two resolution or verify the applicable KU addendum, not discard it based on an E∞ lift alone.
The bound uses d framing coordinates. These hypotheses are a common domain of the particular canonical and trace constructions, not a selection of filtrations on all smooth rings.
The comparison on qΩ is complete; the chosen pair on uncompleted qdR is obtained by the specified pullback.
proofSteps: Import the full framed KU 6.10 comparison from RT.4:q-Hodge (request HT-RT-framed). It identifies the shifted trace graded filtration with the coordinate subcomplex and is constructed using the framed Čech resolution of KU 6.12–6.13.

Use the exact Part I framed-and-fixed-point-descriptions-of-the-canonical-filtration map: the truncation counit with its fixed pullback identification gives F_can→F_frame, reducing to the identity on the Hodge filtration. Completeness then proves this particular map is an equivalence.

Compose these specified maps on the completed coordinate model, then apply the Part I pullback-to-qdR construction. Carry the zeroth-step, mod-β, rational and p-rational identifications and their coherences through the defining pullbacks.
Apply traceHabiro_pairEquiv, equivalently the imported H functor on this equivalence of pairs. This gives the Habiro comparison without using an unproved uncompleted framed Koszul presentation.

sources.locator: Example 6.7, p.82; Theorem 6.10, p.83, proof via 6.11–6.13, pp.84–86; Remark 6.14, p.86
sources.match: The framed smooth spherical lift yields the explicit coordinate filtration and its coherent multiplicative comparison.

sources.locator: Example 3.12, pp.25–26; Remark 3.6, p.22; Remark 4.4, p.55, Lemma 4.7, p.56
sources.match: The coordinate filtration pulls back to a chosen pair; the canonical construction has the same truncated defining pullback on this input class.

acceptance: For S=ℤ[1/2][x], the explicit lift is the flat spherical polynomial algebra S[1/2][x]; all three filtrations compare through the displayed coordinate subcomplex.
For d=0 the framing is étale: F^i=h^max(i,0)S[[h]], and the Habiro output is the relative Habiro ring.
For the polynomial q-Hodge complex M over ℤ, H⁰(M/^Lh)=ℤ[x] whereas H⁰(M)/h=ℤ. The difference is carried by H¹(M)[h], so passing cohomology through reduction is not a comparison proof.
The independent one-variable canonical domain includes ℤ[x], but its square ℤ[x,y] requires 2 to be inverted. The theorem does not silently enlarge this domain using tensor products.
The Laurent example over ℚ still distinguishes uncompleted qdR from qΩ; the completed comparison cannot erase that distinction.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic and Taylor maps on the number-field trace realization
nodes.statement: For any number field F and positive integer Δ divisible by 6 and disc(F), put R=O_F[1/Δ], let S_R be its unique étale spherical lift, and put P_R = π₀(lim_{m, divisibility} ((THH(KU⊗S_R/KU)^{genuine C_m})^{h(S¹/C_m)})). Import the RT ring isomorphism ε_R:H_R≃P_R. Define the cyclotomic reduction ρ_m:P_R→qW_m(R/ℤ[1/Δ]) and the completed Taylor map τ_m:P_R→R[ζ_m][[q−ζ_m]] by composing ε_R^(−1) with the existing Habiro maps. Here H_R is the existing arithmetic ring with its Frobenius-twisted coefficient conventions. These maps satisfy the imported transition, completion and Frobenius-gluing laws, transported through ε_R. They identify P_R with the same Taylor equalizer as H_R and give P_R^∧_h≃R[[h]].
hypotheses: The realization uses periodic KU. First take genuine C_m fixed points, then residual S¹/C_m homotopy fixed points, then the divisibility-indexed limit in spectra, and finally π₀. Neither homotopy C_m fixed points nor a limit of the separate π₀ groups can replace these steps without a separate theorem.
R is finite étale over ℤ[1/Δ]. The coefficient-ring construction requires only discriminant inversion, whereas this RT realization also requires 2 and 3 inverted.
Use the existing absolute number-field/relative Habiro identification and chosen roots for the Taylor factors. Its Frobenius twists and p-adic re-expansions remain part of the gluing data.
No K₃-indexed module, regulator line or higher cohomology comparison is asserted by this degree-zero ring export.
proofSteps: Import RT.4:Habiro-comparison/etale-einfty-lift and /number-field-habiro (KU 6.15); this supplies ε_R with precisely the fixed-point order above. The theorem is not reproved here.

Use HabiroRings HR.5 and HR.6’s equivalence with the existing arithmetic Habiro ring, its q-Witt reductions, completed cyclotomic factors and Frobenius-twisted Taylor equalizer. For the étale Hodge identification use QH Corollary 3.13, not the incorrect 3.12 cross-reference in KU.

Compose each existing specialization with ε_R^(−1). Each diagram commutes by cancellation of ε_R with its inverse; naturality is asserted for the compatible arithmetic/étale maps for which the supplied ε is natural.

Transport the completion equivalences and the joint Taylor equalizer description through the ring isomorphism, keeping p-adic gluing and Frobenius action on coefficients. Do not invent a componentwise constant R-algebra structure.

sources.match: The existing arithmetic Habiro ring is π₀ of this precise genuine-fixed-point/residual-circle divisibility limit under 6·disc(F) inversion.
Étale Habiro-Hodge cohomology is the existing relative Habiro ring; this is the correct cross-reference for KU 6.15.
The target coefficient ring is the Frobenius-twisted Taylor equalizer, with p-adic re-expansion at adjacent roots of unity.

acceptance: For F=ℚ and Δ=6, R=ℤ[1/6], this exports the ordinary Habiro coefficient maps after localization. The m=1 Taylor completion is ℤ[1/6][[h]].
The native unit Check proves that 6 invertible forces 2 and 3 invertible; the source still requires the discriminant condition for arbitrary F.

At every m, ρ_m is the transported q-Witt reduction and the completed map has the same source completion as H_R. The product of Taylor series is the twisted equalizer, rather than arbitrary independent series.
A number field need not admit an embedding as constant Taylor families: Frobenius moves coefficients. All number fields are allowed, including nonabelian F, through the twisted gluing.
Discriminant-only localization is not enough to invoke this theorem; no statement for higher homotopy or arithmetic regulator modules follows from ε_R.

api.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports
api.statement: Transport the existing arithmetic Habiro cyclotomic and Taylor maps along the specified ring isomorphism ε_R:H_R≃P_R.

api.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_cyclotomic
api.statement: ρ_m = reduction_m ∘ ε_R^(−1), with target qW_m(R/ℤ[1/Δ]); the compatible completed target is H_{R,m}.

api.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_taylor
api.statement: τ_m = Taylor_m ∘ ε_R^(−1) into the m-th root expansion factor, using the specified choice ζ_m and its already supplied change-of-root maps.

api.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_transition
api.statement: Cyclotomic transitions and Taylor re-expansions commute with ε_R; the same Frobenius-twisted p-adic gluing equations characterize the family (τ_m(z))_m.

api.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_equalizer
api.statement: The product of τ_m identifies P_R with the existing twisted Taylor equalizer H_R. The equality is inherited from HR.5; no componentwise constant coefficient embedding is added.

api.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_hCompletion
api.statement: The h-completion of P_R is R[[h]], and its projection is τ_1. All (q^m−1)- and Φ_m-completion descriptions are the transported HR.5 descriptions.

api.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_naturality
api.statement: For compatible maps of localized étale arithmetic inputs for which ε is natural, the squares for ρ_m and τ_m commute, with identity and composition laws inherited from the existing Habiro maps.

uses.how: Makes the ring comparison usable for the existing cyclotomic and Taylor tests, preserving the source coefficient gluing.
Supplies a degree-zero trace realization of the coefficient-specialization maps consumed by arithmetic modules; the modules themselves remain with their owner.
Tests candidate arithmetic series through the same completed root expansions without inferring any higher cohomology realization.

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_rational
tests.statement: For F=ℚ, Δ=6, the m=1 Taylor map after h-completion identifies the output with ℤ[1/6][[h]]; h maps to the formal parameter.

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_mOne
tests.statement: At m=1, ζ₁=1 and qW₁(R/ℤ[1/Δ])=R. The reduction of τ₁ at h=0 equals ρ₁, not the whole uncompleted ring P_R.

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_twisted
tests.statement: A family that is constant a∈R in every Taylor component need not satisfy gluing when a is moved by an unramified Frobenius. Treating H_R as an R-algebra of all constant families would admit such a family incorrectly.

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_gluing
tests.statement: The τ_m family lies in the HR.5 Frobenius-twisted re-expansion equalizer, and every such family comes from one P_R element. An unrestricted product of expansion rings fails this test.

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_inversion
tests.statement: The base ring for F=ℚ with Δ=1 satisfies the coefficient discriminant condition but not the KU 6.15 inversion condition. This construction cannot invoke ε_R there.

tests.name: TauCeti.QHodge.Trace.numberFieldTraceExports_degreeZero
tests.statement: ε_R is a ring equivalence with π₀ of the spectral limit. Moving π₀ inside the limit, replacing genuine fixed points by homotopy fixed points, or extending to K₃-indexed modules is not part of this interface.

requests.need: Add the full framed smooth comparison of KU 6.10 (p.83, proof pp.84–86) for a perfectly covered spherical cyclotomic Λ-base and every étale framing A[x₁,…,x_d]→S of KU 6.7. The existing raksit-polynomial-example node states only ℤ[x]. Supply the particular coordinate comparison and its pair coherences, including the applicable 2-adic coherent resolution/addendum verification; keep the h-complete object separate from the pulled-back uncompleted pair. Own it in RT, not Part II.

Make KU 1.11 (p.5) an explicit imported boundary contract: the perfection of the free p-complete δ-ring modulo its generator has an E₁ ku-lift while its ordinary-preimage naive filtration fails the q-deformation condition (the algebraic failure is already Part I HQ.5). No E₂ ku-counterexample or image-of-J comparison theorem is asserted; the latter lacks the required S¹-equivariant diagram. Include the structured quotient range in QH 4.23 (p.63): exponents ≥2 for odd p, even ≥4 at 2. Do not copy the algebraic counterexample into RT.

Expose the existing PR.3 scope as precise nodes for Frobenius-divisibility Nygaard on QRSP covers and its quasisyntomic descent, independently of trace. In the relative bounded-prism smooth setting use Δ^(1)=φ_A^*Δ, the divided Frobenius, graded Hodge–Tate truncations and the Lη_I factorization of BS 15.3 (pp.103–104). Distinguish this object from its Nygaard completion. This supports the imported RT.6 trace-prismatic-comparison and the Part II independent-construction acceptance test; no new prismatic construction is proposed here.

remaining: Supplier contracts HT-RT-boundary and HT-PR-independent must be represented by their owner nodes before marking this stage closed. All moved targets and Checks are routed.
Supplier contract HT-RT-framed must be represented by its full framed comparison node before marking this stage closed. All arithmetic export targets and Checks are routed.

importedTargets.detail: All of the absolute and relative trace-existence statements, full base Frobenius structure, per-prime E₂/E₁ choices and R2 stay RT-owned; consume the complete output pair here.
Import the algebraic failure from Part I and request only the ku-lift/warning boundary from RT. Retain the lack of a known E₂-ku counterexample and the missing S¹ diagram for image-of-J.
